questions.stem: A chemical company uses copper in its products. Copper ore is becoming scarcer and more expensive to mine. Which approach best demonstrates sustainable use of copper?

options.text: Mining faster to stockpile copper before it runs out
Recycling copper from electronic waste, using phytomining to extract copper from low-grade ores, and developing alternative materials
Switching to a different metal without considering its supply
Reducing the quality of products to use less copper

questions.explanation: Sustainability means meeting current needs without compromising future generations. For copper, this involves multiple strategies: recycling (copper retains its properties), phytomining (using plants to absorb copper from low-grade ores), bioleaching (using bacteria to extract copper), and developing alternative materials. Mining faster would deplete resources more quickly and is the opposite of sustainable.

questions.stem: Life cycle assessments (LCAs) compare the environmental impact of products from 'cradle to grave'. A paper bag requires more energy to manufacture than a plastic bag. Does this mean plastic bags are more sustainable?

options.text: Yes, less manufacturing energy always means more sustainable
Not necessarily — an LCA must also consider raw material extraction, transport, lifespan, reusability, and end-of-life disposal; paper bags are biodegradable while plastic bags persist for centuries
Paper bags and plastic bags are equally sustainable
Neither type of bag has any environmental impact

questions.explanation: A full LCA considers all stages: raw materials (oil vs. trees), manufacturing energy, transport, number of uses, and disposal. Paper bags use more energy to make but come from renewable trees, are biodegradable, and are easily recycled. Plastic bags use less energy but come from non-renewable oil, persist for centuries in the environment, and harm wildlife. The most sustainable option is a reusable bag used many times.

questions.stem: A country generates most of its electricity from coal. It plans to replace coal power with wind turbines and solar panels. Why is this transition considered more sustainable even though manufacturing turbines and panels requires energy?

options.text: Wind and solar produce more electricity than coal
Once installed, wind and solar use renewable energy sources, produce no CO₂ during operation, and the initial energy cost is repaid within a few years
Coal will never run out
Wind turbines and solar panels last forever

questions.explanation: Although manufacturing wind turbines and solar panels requires energy (and produces CO₂), this 'embodied energy' is typically repaid within 1-4 years of operation. After that, they generate clean electricity for 20-30+ years using renewable energy (wind and sunlight) without burning finite fossil fuels or producing greenhouse gases during operation. Coal is finite and produces significant CO₂.

questions.stem: Sustainable development aims to meet present needs without compromising future generations. Which of the following is NOT an example of sustainable practice in chemistry?

options.text: Using catalysts to reduce energy requirements in industrial processes
Extracting all remaining fossil fuels as quickly as possible to maximise current economic growth
Developing biodegradable plastics from plant-based materials
Designing manufacturing processes that produce less waste

questions.explanation: Rapidly extracting all fossil fuels prioritises current needs at the expense of future generations — the definition of unsustainable practice. Sustainable approaches include using catalysts (less energy), biodegradable materials (less pollution), and reducing waste (less resource depletion). Sustainability requires balancing economic, environmental, and social needs across generations.

questions.stem: Bioplastics made from corn starch are promoted as sustainable alternatives to oil-based plastics. A critic points out that growing corn for bioplastics uses agricultural land. What does this illustrate about sustainability decisions?

options.text: Bioplastics are always worse than oil-based plastics
Sustainability involves complex trade-offs; using farmland for bioplastics may compete with food production, and all impacts must be weighed
The critic is wrong — land use is not a sustainability concern
We should stop making all plastics entirely

questions.explanation: Sustainability decisions rarely have simple answers. While bioplastics reduce dependence on fossil fuels and are biodegradable, growing crops for bioplastics uses land, water, and fertilisers that could be used for food. A complete LCA must weigh all factors: resource use, land competition, carbon footprint, end-of-life disposal, and social impacts. The best solution depends on local circumstances.
